title: Structural and biochemical investigations of a HEAT-repeat protein involved in the cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly pathway
abstract: Iron-sulfur clusters are essential for life and defects in their biosynthesis lead to human diseases. The mechanism of cluster assembly and delivery to cytosolic and nuclear client proteins via the cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly (CIA) pathway is not well understood. Here we report cryo-EM structures of the HEAT-repeat protein Met18 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a key component of the CIA targeting complex (CTC) that identifies cytosolic and nuclear client proteins and delivers a mature iron-sulfur cluster. We find that in the absence of other CTC proteins, Met18 adopts tetrameric and hexameric states. Using mass photometry and negative stain EM, we show that upon the addition of Cia2, these higher order oligomeric states of Met18 disassemble. We also use pulldown assays to identify residues of critical importance for Cia2 binding and recognition of the Leu1 client, many of which are buried when Met18 oligomerizes. Our structures show conformations of Met18 that have not been previously observed in any Met18 homolog, lending support to the idea that a highly flexible Met18 may be key to how the CTC is able to deliver iron-sulfur clusters to client proteins of various sizes and shapes, i.e. Met18 conforms to the dimensions needed.

narrative_llm:
Short impact summary

This 2023 open-access study provides an early but meaningful signal of scholarly uptake for a structural and biochemical analysis of Met18, a HEAT-repeat protein in the cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly pathway. The paper has been cited 7 times and shows 8 documented downstream reuse events, with follow-on work appearing in journals such as the Journal of the American Chemical Society, Journal of Biological Chemistry, ACS Chemical Biology, Cells, and Biological Chemistry.

Full narrative

Vasquez and colleagues address an important mechanistic gap in iron-sulfur biology: how the cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly pathway supports cluster delivery to client proteins in the cytosol and nucleus. Using cryo-EM and biochemical approaches, the paper focuses on Met18 from Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a key component of the cytosolic targeting complex, and helps clarify a protein system central to fundamental cell biology and disease-relevant iron-sulfur metabolism.

The article is already visible in the citation record of a specialized but credible audience. Its 7 citations are concentrated in 2024–2026 and are drawing on venues that are highly aligned with the paper’s topic, including high-profile chemistry and biochemistry journals. That pattern suggests the work is being used as a structural and mechanistic reference point for later studies of cytosolic iron-sulfur cluster assembly rather than remaining confined to a narrow niche.

The downstream literature also reinforces that interpretation. Subsequent papers cite this study in work on the CIA pathway itself, including analyses of client recruitment and targeting-complex interactions, as well as broader discussions of iron-sulfur protein biogenesis. The reuse record shows that the article is not only being cited in research articles but is also being incorporated into related scholarly writing and synthesis.

Open-access availability is likely helping this reach: the article is deposited in multiple open instances, including PubMed and DOAJ, which supports broad accessibility. The funding record shows substantial support from NIH/NIGMS, NSF, and HHMI-linked support, consistent with a well-resourced structural biology effort. Overall, the record points to a focused, early-stage impact profile: modest in citation volume so far, but with clear uptake in the specific research communities most likely to build on its mechanistic findings.

What is most notable at this stage is the specificity of the response rather than its scale. The paper is being used by researchers working on iron-sulfur cluster biogenesis, protein interactions in the CIA machinery, and related structural questions. That makes it an influential contribution within its specialty, even as the citation base is still developing.
